title: Redo PDF Upload Integration

requirements.text: Rewrite the backend PDF storage and upload logic in main.mo to use a reliable chunked upload approach: split incoming PDF binary data into small chunks (e.g., 500 KB each), store chunks separately in stable memory, and reassemble on retrieval. Expose backend functions: startUpload(title, shareId, totalChunks), uploadChunk(shareId, chunkIndex, chunkData), finalizeUpload(shareId), getPdfChunks(shareId) returning chunk count and metadata, getPdfChunk(shareId, chunkIndex) returning a single chunk blob, listPdfs(), deletePdf(shareId), and renamePdf(shareId, newTitle). Ensure all existing metadata fields (title, shareId, uploadTimestamp) are preserved.

quotes: What if you just redid the pdf Integration

acceptanceCriteria: A 0.39 MB PDF can be uploaded successfully without error
PDFs larger than 2 MB can be uploaded via chunking without failure
Uploaded PDFs can be retrieved in full by shareId
listPdfs() returns correct metadata for all stored PDFs
deletePdf() and renamePdf() continue to work correctly

requirements.text: Rewrite the frontend PDF upload flow in UploadPage.tsx to use the new chunked upload backend API. On file selection, split the PDF ArrayBuffer into chunks of 500 KB, call startUpload to initialize, then sequentially call uploadChunk for each chunk with retry logic (up to 3 retries per chunk on failure), then call finalizeUpload. Display a progress bar showing chunk upload progress (e.g., '3 of 7 chunks uploaded'). Show a clear error message with the specific failure reason if any step fails, and allow the user to retry the upload.

quotes: What if you just redid the pdf Integration

acceptanceCriteria: Uploading a 0.39 MB PDF completes successfully and shows the shareable link
Uploading a PDF larger than 2 MB completes successfully via chunked upload
A progress bar is visible during upload showing chunk progress
A descriptive error message is displayed if upload fails at any step
The user can retry a failed upload without refreshing the page

requirements.text: Rewrite the frontend PDF retrieval and rendering flow in ViewerPage.tsx to use the new chunked retrieval backend API. Fetch the chunk count via getPdfChunks(shareId), then sequentially fetch each chunk via getPdfChunk(shareId, chunkIndex), reassemble all chunks into a single Blob, create an object URL, and render the PDF in an iframe. Show a loading progress indicator while chunks are being fetched. Display a clear error message if retrieval fails.

quotes: What if you just redid the pdf Integration

acceptanceCriteria: A previously uploaded PDF renders correctly in the iframe on the viewer page
A loading indicator is shown while chunks are being assembled
An error message is displayed if the PDF cannot be retrieved
The PDF title is displayed at the top of the page
The 'Next PDF' navigation button continues to function correctly

requirements.text: Update the React Query hooks in useQueries.ts to expose the new chunked upload and chunked retrieval functions, replacing the old single-call upload and fetch hooks. Ensure the dashboard list, delete, and rename hooks continue to work with the updated backend API signatures.

quotes: What if you just redid the pdf Integration

acceptanceCriteria: useQueries.ts exposes hooks for chunked upload (startUpload, uploadChunk, finalizeUpload)
useQueries.ts exposes hooks for chunked retrieval (getPdfChunks, getPdfChunk)
Dashboard list, delete, and rename operations continue to function correctly
No references to the old single-call upload/fetch API remain in the hooks file

constraints: All backend logic must remain in backend/main.mo (single-actor architecture)
Do not modify files under frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, or frontend/src/components/ui
Preserve all existing metadata fields: title, shareId, uploadTimestamp
Chunk size must not exceed 500 KB to stay within IC message size limits
nonGoals: Changing the visual theme or UI styling
Modifying the logo or header/footer components
